claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 11 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask:

**Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation), and if so, how much do you contribute and how often?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes and other bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if your contributions are sufficient for Child Benefit eligibility, I need to know more specifically:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (for example, weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £26.05 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**How long has Alex been living away from you - is it more or less than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living away from me for quite a while now - more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✓ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 11 years old, which is under 16

✓ **UK residency**: You live in the UK

✓ **Responsibility for the child**: Although Alex doesn't live with you, you are considered responsible for him because you contribute £26.05 per week towards his upkeep. This meets the requirement of paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent) for things like clothes and other necessities

✓ **No competing claim**: No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

✓ **Sufficient contributions**: Even though Alex has been living away from you for more than 8 weeks, your ongoing weekly contributions equal to or exceeding the Child Benefit amount mean you can continue to receive Child Benefit beyond the initial 8-week period

You should be able to apply for Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can do so through the official government channels.
